argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification for launch readiness on a caveated basis, not as a clean no-limitation certification. Aggregate readiness clears by 2.3 percentage points, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general support, latency, and rollback checks passed. The same record also shows that chargeback evidence summarization is a named deployment context whose evals are not in the packet, so that context must be presented as an unknown with an explicit disclosed evaluation gap. The narrow defensible position is therefore: certification is supportable if and only if the packet/model card carries that limitation statement, and the draft 'no known merchant dispute support limitations' language should not be relied on.
claims_about_business_cost: The remaining issue is a bounded disclosure and framing issue, not a failure of the demonstrated general launch-readiness checks. Treating it as a caveated-compliance issue avoids turning a remediable documentation overclaim into a broader escalation where the admissible evidence already supports a narrower, policy-aligned certification position.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not require withholding certification whenever any named-context eval is incomplete; it requires disclosure or resolution of the material limitation or evaluation gap before clean certification. On this record, general readiness evidence is enough to support launch readiness, but it is not enough to support an unconditional no-limitation statement. The policy-consistent treatment is caveated certification with explicit disclosure of the chargeback evidence summarization gap.
concessions: The present record does not support any claim of clean certification with no deployment limitation.
The draft statement that there are no known merchant dispute support limitations is not supported on the current evidence.
The record does not show chargeback evidence summarization as a passed launch capability.
If the required disclosure is not actually included in the final packet or model card, the support for certification is incomplete under policy.
